newsitem.title: GERMANY: IWKA says sees 97 profit gain likely.
newsitem.headline: IWKA says sees 97 profit gain likely.

text.p: German machinery and plant construction group IWKA AG said on Friday gains from consolidating its holdings were likely to push 1997 profit above its net income total reported a year ago.
Sales for the full year were also exepcted to rise, after sales and orders had a mixed showing in the first half, the company said at its annual meeting.
Higher sales would probably boost net profit above last year's 40.7 million marks, chief executive Hans Fahr said.
Including results from consolidated units, IWKA's first-half sales rose 31 percent to 1.382 billion marks. On a comparable basis without subsidiaries' results, sales fell three percent, IWKA said.
Consolidated orders in the first half rose 10 percent to 1.555 billion marks -- but on a comparable basis fell 10 percent to 1.271 billion marks.
IWKA has consolidated machine tool maker Ex-Cell-O Holding AG, in which it holds a 65 percent stake, as well as Usines Farman SA and defence group Henschel Wehrtechnik GmbH.
The move should lead to a reduction in losses at Ex-Cell-O, although costs from resturcturing Henschel would still have a negative impact on profit, Fahr said.
Last year IWKA reported unconsolidated sales rose 24 percent to 2.6 billion marks while net income increased 48 percent to 40.7 million marks.
